correctness.rationale: Faber–Pandharipande coefficient identity and direct partition expansion reduce the claim to a complete p-adic valuation comparison. For t=q-f≥1 all summands have denominator valuation at most E−1; for t=0 length is ≤m, and equality length m forces λ*=(1^r,s^q). Its unique leading summand computes the Wilson residue, with no cancellation. Monic integral rising factorials and 4^{-g} shift preserve leading degree and p-integrality. A standalone exact rational check passed 206 prime/genus instances. Boundary q>=1 and p>=5 explicit.

originality.rationale: Holmes (arXiv:2610.30274v1, §3.1) establishes the p-adic lcm and partition uniqueness at a selected length, not the explicit index cutoff/residue stated here; extending the valuation argument to all greater lengths yields a distinct exact prime-by-prime individual-integral assertion. Three dedicated semantic database queries, one broader query, current accessible local ledger and primary paper comparisons found no equivalent statement. An implicit result in earlier Nörlund arithmetic remains a documented priority risk.
residual_risks: Holmes Lemma 3.5 contains nearly all needed valuation inequalities; the cutoff may be viewed as implicit rather than new in an expanded mathematical sense.
Adelberg (1999) full text was not read; a Nörlund polynomial congruence might imply the residue/cutoff.
Faber–Pandharipande 1998 and 2003 primary full texts were not inspected; reliance on the exact identity stated in Holmes is explicit.
Historical priority cannot be established from semantic database retrieval, especially unindexed results.

value.rationale: The genus-wise denominator theorem does not locate the minimal Chern-Hodge index λ_{g-i} among one-point tautological intersections attaining the prime extremum; this natural graded-support threshold is exactly q(s−1), and its residue is nonzero. It is a uniform structural identification across infinitely many genera and primes rather than an arbitrary numerical sample or a re-expression of the lcm. The result is closely tied to Holmes and historical priority remains a risk.
